articleTitle: The way forward for knowledge elicitation-psychologist or engineer?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Sources and Training of Knowledge Engineers
abstract: The key features of knowledge engineering which distinguish it from more conventional systems design are outlined, and some of the skills which are useful in knowledge engineering are described. Some suggestions for developing such skills are also proposed. For those who are happy to study unfamiliar subjects and who are prepared to cope with and under uncertainty there are many prospects. It is almost certain that a willingness to learn and ask questions of other people is more important than any particular subject background. There is a clear need for more organized training of knowledge engineers. In the longer term it may be necessary to revise undergraduate programmes to include more material from nontechnical but highly relevant subjects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software package to assist the knowledge elicitation engineer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Sources and Training of Knowledge Engineers
abstract: The LUKE system is a knowledge structuring tool which is easy for any user to use. The system imposes a rigid structure onto the knowledge base which can only be effectively implemented in diagnostic applications. If the expert system can be investigated separately as a series of small scale activities, then LUKE may become more flexible. The complete expert system can be built by the knowledge engineer by linking small-scale prototype expert systems together to obtain the full solution. An exercise using LUKE has been carried out to determine the suitability of a computer workstation for a job. Further studies are being carried out into process control. LUKE provides a useful mechanism for the rapid prototyping of diagnostic expert systems. It is hoped that the LUKE system will be made commercially available in the next few years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Sources and Training of Knowledge Engineers
abstract: Describes a 10-week study programme in knowledge-based systems (KBS), developed on the basis of experience by Edinburgh University. It is in two stages. Stage I is concerned with breadth training and comprises a number of intensive practical-based courses on methodologies and techniques. Stage II is concerned with depth training where the knowledge engineer is required to specify and build a KBS which is specific to his or her organisation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of new technology on engineering training
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Sources and Training of Knowledge Engineers
abstract: The potential of using expert systems for producing computer-based tutoring systems is very promising. To make proper use of new technology in training, an expert system has been proposed which has the case setup environment, solution analysis environment, and consultation environment. The case setup environment aids the user in selecting the type of case to be made and the objective of the study, and, finally, the selection of the constraints for this type of study. The system consists of training preparation, training session, and training playback modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
